title: Chapter 67 — Cutting In
paragraphs: It was a Saturday night, and such a Sabbath as followed! By their very profession, all whalemen are breakers of the Sabbath. The ivory Pequod was turned into what seemed a slaughterhouse. Every sailor was a butcher. You would have thought we were sacrificing ten thousand red oxen to the sea gods.

In the first place, the enormous cutting tackles — among other heavy items, a cluster of blocks generally painted green, which no single man can possibly lift — this vast bunch of equipment was hoisted up to the main-top and firmly lashed to the lower masthead, the strongest point anywhere above a ship's deck. The end of the heavy rope was then pulled aft, and after going through various blocks, was fastened to a great iron ring bolted into the deck near the bow. When all was ready, a broad, semicircular line was cut through the whale's body on both sides. This cut marked the outline of the first enormous strip of blubber — called a blanket-piece — that was about to be stripped from the whale's body. An enormous hook was then inserted at the edge of this strip, and the tackle was heaved tight. Then the ship rolled toward the whale, and the heavy tackles strained and creaked. Slowly, and with a noise like the tearing of sails, the great blanket-piece began to peel away from the body. The ship leaned harder and harder to the whale, until the hook pulled higher and the strip tore longer. At last, with one mighty wrench, the tackle swung free, and a great sheet of blubber, five feet wide and thirty feet long, hung from the hook like a huge pendulum.

One of the attending harpooners now advanced with a long, keen weapon called a boarding-sword, and watching his chance, he skillfully sliced a large hole in the lower part of the swaying mass. Into this hole, the end of the second tackle's hook was inserted to maintain hold on the blubber, in preparation for what was called the "Bible leaves" cut. For just as Bible leaves are connected at the spine, so the blanket-pieces, in preparation for being lowered into the blubber-room, were attached by a thin strip that allowed them to fold like pages. The enormous mass was then lowered into the ship's hold. Meanwhile the first tackle, now freed, was hoisted to begin stripping the next piece. In this way, the whale was stripped of his blubber as an orange is peeled in a spiral.
